# Project brief: EPW NailBase CI-50 pilot house

**From:** Mira Okafor, Technical Director, Example Panel Works Ltd. *(fictional)*
**Date:** 2026-10-12  **To:** "whoever approves building products in Alberta"

## What we want
Our panel is selling in two other provinces. We want **approval to sell it across Alberta** and a first **pilot house** in Edmonton this spring. Builders love it because vinyl siding nails **straight into the facer**, so there's no OSB and no strapping.

## The product (see the data sheet)
- 50 mm rigid foam core with a 6 mm fibre-cement nail-base facer, factory-bonded. No wood content.
- Shiplap edges. We tape the joints with our own tape.
- Replaces 11 mm OSB on 2×6 walls at 400 mm o.c.

## Pilot house
| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Builder | Birchfield Example Homes *(fictional)*, contact Dev Rahman |
| Owner | "The buyer, not decided yet". Builder-owned spec home until sale |
| Address | 0000 Example Way NW, Edmonton, AB *(fictional)* |
| Legal description | *Don't have it* |
| Permit # | *Not applied yet* |
| Building | 2-storey single-family, about 190 m², unsprinklered, HRV planned |
| Wall, inside to out | 12.7 mm gypsum, poly, 2×6 studs with batts, **NailBase CI-50**, housewrap? (*maybe not needed*), vertical vinyl siding nailed to facer |

## What we have
1. Product data sheet (ours)
2. Permeance test summary from a lab in the US *(EXAMPLE)*
3. Draft letter from our consulting engineer about nail pull-out *(EXAMPLE, not signed yet)*
4. In-house wind-load pull-out tests (spreadsheet, not attached)

## What we don't have yet
- Any CCMC or other evaluation report. We "started an enquiry".
- Air-leakage test, a bracing design, and a flame-spread / foam-protection argument.

## Our questions
1. How do we get approved for all of Alberta?
2. Can the pilot house go ahead on a variance while we wait?
3. Do we need an engineer to stamp anything?
note: The pilot-house row writes 2-storey, single-family, and about 190 m². factory-bonded is not an occupancy. 50 mm is panel thickness. alternative_description was relabelled with the clause rule after the fix and is not a blind label.

# Project brief: Example Commons, firestop issue on L3–L4

**From:** Carlos Mendes, PM, Northgate Example Builders Ltd. *(fictional)*  **Date:** 2026-10-15

## Project
| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Name | Example Commons *(fictional)* |
| Address | 0000 Example Avenue SW, Calgary, AB *(fictional)* |
| Legal | Lot 0, Block 0, Plan 0000000 *(fictional placeholder)* |
| Owner | Example Commons Holdings Inc. *(fictional)* |
| Building permit | BP-0000-00000 *(fictional)*, issued |
| Building | 5 storeys, sprinklered, retail at grade, 64 dwelling units above |
| Design team | Example Architecture Inc. *(fictional)*, coordinating registered professional; Example MEP Engineering *(fictional)* |
| Floor assemblies | Rated fire separations. *Rating per the architect's code analysis: "1 h"* |

## What happened
Our firestop sub sealed the plumbing penetrations on L3 and L4 with **Example FireSeal 200** *(fictional)* and handed in listing **EX-FS-1234** *(fictional)*. The third-party firestop inspector says that listing only covers **metal pipes**. Ours are mostly **PVC drain pipe and bundles of PEX**, and some holes are bigger than the listing allows. L2 (copper) passed.

The sprinkler fitter used the same sealant around the sprinkler branch lines. The sub says sprinklers are "exempt".

## What we need
- Keep the **drywall close-in on 2026-10-24**
- Ideally "a variance so we don't have to rip it out"
- We have a **draft EJ email** from the sealant rep

## Who we've talked to
- Architect (email attached). Not yet the City inspector.
note: The building row writes 5 storeys. Retail at grade and dwelling units are not a single occupancy word in the extractor list. No area or span is written.

# Project brief: Example Crescent infill house

**From:** Priya Natarajan, Larkspur Example Homes *(fictional)*  **Date:** 2026-10-16

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Address | 0000 Example Crescent NW, Edmonton, AB *(fictional)* |
| Legal | Lot 0, Block 0, Plan 0000000 *(fictional placeholder)* |
| Owner (client) | J. & R. Example *(fictional)* |
| Builder / applicant | Larkspur Example Homes *(fictional)* |
| Building | Detached single-family, 2 storeys, ~210 m², no suite, **no sprinklers** |
| Permit | Not yet applied for |
| Designer | In-house drafting (no architect or engineer of record yet). Truss and spray-foam suppliers to be confirmed. |

## Design features we think are "different"
1. **No basement.** A slab-on-grade with in-floor hydronic heat. We want **R-7.5 rigid insulation** under the slab (the code table says more; we heard there's a STANDATA).
2. **Flat-look roof** (low slope) with **no attic vents**. Closed-cell spray foam sprayed under the roof deck, with batts below.
3. **Bedroom 3 "slot" window:** the client loves a tall, narrow casement on the street side. Clear opening per the supplier is **400 mm wide × 780 mm high**. It's the only window in that bedroom.

## Ask
Tell us what needs a variance, and draft whatever's needed so we can apply for the permit by mid-November.
